title: fNIRS in autism neuroscience: From replication to discovery
title_zh: 功能近红外光谱在自闭症神经科学中的应用：从复制到发现
abstract: Studying the neural basis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has long been hampered by a mismatch: core social features unfold during interaction, whereas standard neuroimaging commonly relies on isolated, scanner-based environments. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) partly addresses this mismatch. It is portable, more tolerant of moderate movement than fMRI, and compatible with live social interaction, although it remains sensitive to optode motion and systemic physiology and is restricted primarily to superficial cortex. This narrative review examines three contributions of fNIRS to ASD neuroscience: access to developmental populations that are difficult to study with fMRI; dyadic paradigms that measure neural coordination during live interaction; and integration with behavioral, gaze, autonomic, and electrophysiological signals. We then review wearable and naturalistic systems, machine-learning-based classification, and applications across related neurodevelopmental conditions, while critically appraising small samples, task heterogeneity, and preprocessing variability. Among the 25 reports examined in detail, no classification model had been evaluated in an independent external ASD cohort. Eleven reports linked an fNIRS-derived measure to a clinical, behavioral, or developmental outcome through at least one statistically significant association. These associations were generally exploratory, cross-sectional, and not independently validated. The evidence therefore supports fNIRS as a research tool for cortical hemodynamic measurement, while specific fNIRS-derived patterns of regional activation or connectivity have yet to be validated as biomarkers. Priorities include longitudinal multi-site cohorts, physiologically informed preprocessing, population-specific motion validation, independent model testing, and direct linkage of neural measures to developmental or treatment outcomes.
abstract_zh: 研究自闭症谱系障碍（ASD）的神经基础长期受到不匹配的制约：核心社会特征在互动中展开，而标准神经影像学通常依赖于孤立的、基于扫描仪的环境。功能近红外光谱（fNIRS）在一定程度上解决了这一不匹配。它便携、对中度运动的容忍度高于 fMRI，并且兼容实时社会互动，尽管它仍对光电探头运动和系统生理学敏感，并主要局限于表层皮层。本综述评估了 fNIRS 对 ASD 神经科学的三大贡献：① 进入使用 fMRI 难以研究的发育人群；② 通过双人范式测量实时互动中的神经协调；③ 与行为、注视、交感神经和电生理信号的整合。随后我们回顾了可穿戴和自然主义系统、基于机器学习的分类以及在相关神经发育疾病中的应用，并对样本量小、任务异质性和预处理变异性进行批判性评估。在详细审查的 25 篇报告中，没有任何分类模型在独立的外部 ASD 队列中得到评估。十一篇报告通过至少一次统计显著关联，将 fNIRS 推导的测量与临床、行为或发育结果联系起来。这些关联普遍为探索性、横断面且未经过独立验证。因此，证据支持将 fNIRS 作为皮层血流动力学测量的研究工具，而特定的 fNIRS 推导的区域激活或连接模式尚未被验证为生物标志物。优先事项包括纵向多中心队列、基于生理学的预处理、针对人群的运动验证、独立模型测试，以及将神经测量直接与发育或治疗结果关联。
